sections.title: The pattern behind these bugs
sections.note: Three failure shapes preserved with examples. One example is misattributed: "a 180 degree rather than 90 degree rotation" is the ShaderEffect 3D-route fixture (easygl_shadereffect_3d_test.cpp), not a stock-effect fix (F3).

findings.bible: Bible ch15 GpuDrawParams section: specularEnabled "ignored by every renderer except D3D9" (alpha.1 wording); ledger WP07-ch15-050 records the correction (DIRECTX9 and FNA3D read it).
findings.target: modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp::DrawEnvironmentMapEffect (params.specularEnabled passed to the ShaderIndex helper, and EnvironmentMapSpecular uploaded to the pixel stage) and modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dDraw.cpp (params.specularEnabled in the env-map variant selection) both read the flag; EnvironmentMapEffect::FillGpuDrawParams fills it (setEnvironmentMapSpecularProperty sets specularEnabled_ = colour != 0). Only the header comment in IGraphicsRenderer.hpp still says no renderer reads it (CNA-BUG-261).
findings.site_now: stock-effects-semantics.html#environmentmapeffect (Specular bullet) says the flag is one "which no renderer reads; see the draw packet". The page it points to (effect-object-model.html#draw-packet), docs/effects.html Known issues (CNA-BUG-261) and the ledger all say DIRECTX9 and FNA3D read it. The ledger marked the correction "page corrected" but only one of the two pages was corrected.

fix.old_html: A non-black specular colour also sets the effect's specularEnabled flag (XNA's shader-variant switch), which no renderer reads; see the draw packet.
fix.html: A non-black specular colour also sets the effect's specularEnabled flag (XNA's shader-variant switch). The flag travels in the draw packet and is read by DIRECTX9 (D3D9EffectDraw.cpp) and FNA3D (Fna3dDraw.cpp) to pick XNA's specular shader variant; the other renderers derive the specular term from the colour. The header comment saying no renderer reads it is stale (CNA-BUG-261); see the draw packet.

findings.bible: Not in the Bible (site-authored). Bible DualTexture section only says two independent texture slots and a stride-24 coloured variant.
findings.target: XNA 4.0 refuses a draw whose declaration lacks a semantic the shader reads (FrameworkResources.MissingVertexShaderInput); CNA has no such check (GraphicsDevice::validateDrawState). For a missing TextureCoordinate1: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp::BuildDualTextureVertexLayoutEXT and the stride-20/24 attribute tables (VULKAN-150) point inUV1 at TextureCoordinate0 (dual_texture3d.vert.glsl header: "A record that declares no TextureCoordinate1 has this input pointed at TextureCoordinate0"), while EasyGL/OPENGL4 leave the attribute unbound and read the neutral (0,0,0,1). The site known-issue page CNA-GAP-033 records the same split ("VULKAN aliases TEXCOORD1 onto TEXCOORD0 for DualTextureEffect where the others read (0, 0)").
findings.site_now: stock-effects-semantics.html#dualtextureeffect: "so a mesh with a single UV set samples the second texture at zero." docs/effects.html#dualtextureeffect: "(a single-UV mesh leaves the second set at zero)". Both state one renderer-specific outcome as universal; CNA-GAP-033 (linked from docs/graphics-state.html) says otherwise.

fix.old_html: so a mesh with a single UV set samples the second texture at zero. The shaders double
fix.html: so give the mesh both sets. XNA refuses a draw whose declaration lacks TextureCoordinate1; CNA has no such check (CNA-GAP-033), and what the second texture then sees depends on the renderer: (0, 0) on EasyGL, OPENGL4 and the others, but the first set's coordinates on VULKAN, which aliases TextureCoordinate1 onto TextureCoordinate0 (VULKAN-150). The shaders double

fix.old_html: so the vertex format needs both (a single-UV mesh leaves the second set at zero).
fix.html: so the vertex format needs both (XNA refuses a single-UV draw; CNA does not check, and the second texture reads (0, 0) on most renderers but the first set’s coordinates on VULKAN — see CNA-GAP-033).

findings.bible: Bible ch15 EnvironmentMapEffect history note: "its base and specular terms omitted the cube alpha scale" (ledger WP07-ch15-086: "the base and specular terms include the combined alpha").
findings.target: modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/GlStockShaderSources.hpp (env map fragment): float combinedAlpha=uDiffuseColor.a*texColor.a; rgb = mix(baseColor, envSample.rgb*combinedAlpha, blendFactor) + uEnvMapSpecular*envSample.a*combinedAlpha. XNA reference: modules/renderers/directx9/src/shaders/xna/EnvironmentMapEffect.fx (envmap = SAMPLE_CUBEMAP(...) * color.a; color.rgb += EnvironmentMapSpecular * envmap.a).
findings.site_now: stock-effects-semantics.html#environmentmapeffect: Blend bullet gives lerp(color.rgb, envmap.rgb, weight) with no alpha scaling; Specular bullet says only "EnvironmentMapSpecular multiplied by the cube map's alpha". The combined-alpha factor the ledger recorded is absent, so a translucent reflective surface would be predicted brighter than XNA and CNA render it.

fix.old_html: lerp(color.rgb, envmap.rgb, weight), where the weight is the Fresnel factor times EnvironmentMapAmount.
fix.html: lerp(color.rgb, envmap.rgb, weight), where envmap is the cube sample already scaled by the combined alpha (texture alpha times Alpha, as in XNA) and the weight is the Fresnel factor times EnvironmentMapAmount.

fix.old_html: EnvironmentMapSpecular multiplied by the cube map's alpha.
fix.html: EnvironmentMapSpecular multiplied by the cube map's alpha and by that same combined alpha, added after the blend.

Verified in BlendState.cpp/GraphicsDevice.cpp: shared payload (state_), copy ctor = new unbound payload, operator= = ShareResourceIdentityWith alias, device fields assigned by operator=, BindForUse sets isBound, every setter ThrowIfBound with the message "Cannot modify a BlendState after it has been bound to a GraphicsDevice."; presets are const and pre-bound; identity outlives the local (test AssignedStateIdentitiesOutliveSourcesAndRebindAcrossDevices). sections.note: Example recreated correctly for the frozen model (copy-construct a variant, then assign). setBlendStateProperty order verified: no-op for the active payload unless dirty, ValidateBlendStateForProfile, BindForUse, ApplyBlendState(six ordinals + BlendWriteState), SetBlendFactor, then cache commit. Stale leftover on the user-guide page: "each setter ... copies it" (F3).

Vertex collections reach compiled-effect draws only (GraphicsDevice validate + EasyGL/OPENGL4/SOFTWARE consumers): the page does not name the consumers and the compiled-effects page contradicts it (F1).

fix.old_html: Depth-function evidence is narrower: easygl_depthstencilstate_compare_function_test.cpp draws five discriminating cases (Always, Never, Less, LessEqual, Greater) and is registered as EasyGL_DepthStencilState_CompareFunction and, from the same source, Vulkan_DepthStencilState_CompareFunction; that is not a sweep of all eight values.
fix.html: Depth-function evidence has two layers. The parity fixture depth_states (registered as <Renderer>_Parity_depth_states for EasyGL, WebGPU, SDL_GPU and OpenGL 4) runs all eight CompareFunctions as an 8×3 matrix of nearer, equal and farther fragments, so no pair of functions shares a signature. The older, narrower test is easygl_depthstencilstate_compare_function_test.cpp, five discriminating cases (Always, Never, Less, LessEqual, Greater) registered as EasyGL_DepthStencilState_CompareFunction and, from the same source, Vulkan_DepthStencilState_CompareFunction; VULKAN is not part of the parity corpus, so for it that five-case test is not a sweep of all eight values.

findings.bible: Bible ch16 intro: "A device assignment copies the supplied state into its own CPU field ... mutating the original local value later cannot change the stored device value." Ledger WP06-ch16-003/004 correct this (assignment aliases; mutation after binding throws).
findings.target: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp::setBlendStateProperty (blendState_ = value; BindForUse) with BlendState::operator= sharing the payload; BlendState::ThrowIfBound. The setter takes const BlendState& and does not copy the fields into a private value.
findings.site_now: docs/graphics-state.html#overview: "Each getter has a reference-returning form and each setter takes the state object by const reference and copies it." This is the Bible's superseded by-value statement, kept on the user-guide page whose own section "Assigned states are frozen" (same page) says the device field and the assigned object share one state.

fix.old_html: Each getter has a reference-returning form and each setter takes the state object by const reference and copies it.

or precompile the exact SPIR-V contract Vulkan expects.

The Vulkan contract (read from VulkanEffectRenderer and VulkanRenderer.cpp; Vulkan_ShaderEffect_SpirV exercises the SpriteBatch route). A batch feeds the shader SpriteBatch’s fixed 32-byte vertex: location 0 a vec2 pixel position, location 1 a vec2 texture coordinate, location 2 a vec4 colour. Scalar uniforms travel in one 128-byte push-constant block visible to both stages: bytes 0–7 are a vec2 viewport size that the batch writes for you (the active viewport’s width and height, or the target or virtual-resolution size when no custom viewport is set), bytes 8–15 are padding, bytes 16–79 one mat4, bytes 80–95 one vec4 and bytes 96–99 one float. Uniform names are not consulted: SetUniformMat4 fills the matrix slot, SetUniformVec4, SetUniformVec3 and SetUniformVec2 fill the leading four, three or two floats of the one vector slot, and SetUniformFloat and SetUniformInt both write the one float slot (the integer converted to float), so a second setter of the same kind overwrites the first. The array setters use uniform-buffer ranges in descriptor set 1, one per element type, again chosen by type rather than name. A 3D draw with a ShaderEffect needs the vertex buffer’s own VertexDeclaration (the layout is never inferred from the stride) and throws NotSupportedException without one; a per-instance stream’s attribute locations continue after the per-vertex elements.

The SDL_GPU contract uses the same fixed-slot, name-ignoring setters but a different SpriteBatch vertex: 36 bytes, a vec3 position at location 0, a vec2 texture coordinate at location 1 and a vec4 colour at location 2. Its 128-byte uniform block is copied to both stages, with a vec4 at bytes 0–15 whose first two floats are the viewport size, then the same matrix (16–79), vector (80–95) and float (96–99) slots; where that block and the sampler live (vertex set 1, fragment sets 3 and 2) is on SDL_GPU: which GLSL the runtime route accepts. The Direct3D sprite vertex is on Custom HLSL ShaderEffect on the Direct3D renderers; the three layouts are not interchangeable.

fix.old_html: SPIR-V words only (.spv bytes in the string); pre-compile with glslc
fix.html: SPIR-V words only (.spv bytes in the string); pre-compile with glslc. Uniform names are not consulted: each setter type fills a fixed slot of the 128-byte push-constant block (see Four shader routes)
